reasoning: Recent polling in Minnesota’s 2026 U.S. Senate general election shows Democrats holding a modest but consistent edge over Republican nominee Michele Tafoya, with most credible surveys putting Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan ahead by mid–single digits and a generic Democrat up by a similar margin.[1][4][11] There is no fresh, state-specific presidential general-election polling in the last 45 days in the gathered results, so the best current quantitative picture is that the Senate race is roughly D+6–8, in line with Minnesota’s slight Democratic lean in partisan index terms, but still competitive.[4][11]

sources.name: The New York Times (Impact Research poll summary)
sources.details: Impact Research poll (reported in NYT aggregation and Newsweek) found Peggy Flanagan leading Michele Tafoya by 7 points, 51% to 44% in a Minnesota U.S. Senate general-election matchup.

sources.name: Yahoo News reporting PPP poll
sources.details: Public Policy Polling survey of Minnesota Democratic primary voters showed Peggy Flanagan leading Angie Craig 46% to 32%, a 14‑point advantage in the DFL Senate primary.

sources.name: KSTP/SurveyUSA
sources.details: SurveyUSA/KSTP poll found the DFL Senate primary between Angie Craig and Peggy Flanagan tied at 40%–40%, indicating a neck‑and‑neck primary but not measuring the general election.

sources.details: Later SurveyUSA/KSTP polling just before the primary showed Angie Craig ahead of Peggy Flanagan 42% to 40% among DFL primary voters, again only reflecting the Democratic primary balance.

sources.details: Official Minnesota Secretary of State primary results show Peggy Flanagan winning the DFL U.S. Senate primary with 59.0% of the vote to Angie Craig’s 39.4%, establishing Flanagan as the Democratic nominee but not indicating general-election margin.
